questions.question: What are the three states of matter?
questions.explanation: Matter can be a solid with a fixed shape, a liquid that flows, or a gas that spreads out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: solids keep their shape, liquids flow, gases fill the room!

questions.question: Which of these is a solid?
questions.explanation: An ice cube keeps its own shape, so it is a solid.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: if it keeps its shape when you pick it up, it is a solid!

questions.question: Which of these is a gas?
questions.explanation: Air spreads out to fill its container and you cannot see it, so it is a gas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: gases are sneaky - they fill every corner!

questions.question: What happens to water when it freezes?
questions.explanation: Freezing cools water until it changes from a liquid into solid ice.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cold turns flowing water into hard ice!

questions.question: What is melting?
questions.correctAnswer: A solid changing into a liquid
distractors: A liquid changing into a solid
A gas changing into a liquid
questions.explanation: When a solid warms up enough, it melts and becomes a liquid.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: heat melts a solid into a puddle!

questions.question: What do we call water changing into water vapor?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when liquid water turns into invisible water vapor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the sun lifts water up into the sky as vapor!

questions.question: Which tool measures the mass of an object?
questions.explanation: A balance scale compares masses, while a ruler measures length.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a balance scale weighs things like a dino seesaw!

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of matter that keeps the properties of an element?
questions.explanation: Atoms are the tiny building blocks of all matter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: atoms are the tiniest dino building blocks!

questions.question: Which of these is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Trail mix is a mixture because its parts stay separate and can be picked apart.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a mixture keeps its parts separate - like trail mix!

questions.question: What happens to the particles of a solid when it is heated?
questions.correctAnswer: They move faster and spread apart
distractors: They turn into atoms of a new element
questions.explanation: Heat gives particles more energy, so they vibrate faster and spread apart.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: heat makes tiny particles dance faster!

questions.question: Which material is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Metals let heat flow through them easily, which is why metal pans get hot.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: metal passes heat along like a hot potato!

questions.question: What is density?
questions.correctAnswer: How much mass is packed into a space
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume - how tightly matter is packed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: density is how squished the mass is inside!

questions.question: Why does ice float on water?
questions.correctAnswer: Ice is less dense than liquid water
questions.explanation: Frozen water spreads out a little, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ice floats because it is lighter for its size than water!

questions.question: Which change is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning makes new substances (ash, smoke) that cannot turn back into wood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: burning makes brand-new stuff - that is a chemical change!

questions.question: What is a solution?
questions.correctAnswer: A mixture where one substance dissolves evenly in another
distractors: A gas trapped in a bottle
questions.explanation: In a solution, like salt water, the dissolved part spreads evenly and cannot be seen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a solution hides the dissolved part completely!

questions.question: Which of these will dissolve fastest in warm water?
distractors: A whole sugar cube in cold water
questions.explanation: Warm water, small pieces, and stirring all speed up dissolving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: warm water plus stirring equals speedy dissolving!

questions.question: What is a producer in an ecosystem?
questions.correctAnswer: An organism that makes its own food, like a plant
distractors: An animal that eats other animals
A fungus that breaks down dead things
questions.explanation: Producers, such as plants, make food using sunlight.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants are the chefs - they cook food from sunlight!

questions.question: What is a consumer?
questions.correctAnswer: An organism that eats other organisms for energy
questions.explanation: Consumers cannot make their own food, so they eat producers or other consumers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: consumers eat to get their energy!

questions.question: What does a decomposer do?
questions.correctAnswer: It breaks down dead plants and animals
questions.explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria recycle nutrients from dead things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: decomposers are nature's clean-up crew!

questions.question: In a food chain, what eats the grass?
questions.explanation: The grasshopper is the herbivore that eats the producer, grass.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: follow the munching - grasshopper eats grass!

questions.question: Which animal is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: A herbivore eats only plants, like a rabbit eating grass and leaves.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: herbivores munch plants all day!

questions.question: Which animal is a carnivore?
questions.explanation: A carnivore eats meat, and a wolf hunts other animals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: carnivores hunt meat for dinner!

questions.question: Which animal is an omnivore?
questions.explanation: An omnivore eats both plants and animals, like a bear eating berries and fish.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: omnivores eat plants AND meat - best of both menus!

questions.question: What is a food web?
questions.correctAnswer: Many food chains linked together in an ecosystem
distractors: A spider's web in a garden
A net used to catch fish
questions.explanation: A food web shows how many food chains connect, since most animals eat more than one thing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a food web is many food chains tangled together!

questions.question: If all the rabbits in a meadow disappeared, what would most likely happen to the foxes?
questions.correctAnswer: The foxes would have less food and their numbers would fall
distractors: The foxes would eat more grass
The foxes would turn into rabbits
questions.explanation: Foxes eat rabbits, so losing that food source means fewer foxes can survive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: take away the prey and the hunters go hungry!

questions.question: What is a habitat?
questions.correctAnswer: The place where an organism lives
questions.explanation: A habitat is the home environment that gives an organism food, water, and shelter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a habitat is an animal's home address!

questions.question: What is an adaptation?
questions.correctAnswer: A trait that helps an organism survive in its home
distractors: A disease that hurts an animal
questions.explanation: Adaptations, like a cactus storing water, help living things survive where they live.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: adaptations are survival superpowers!

questions.question: Why do cacti have thick, waxy stems?
questions.correctAnswer: To store water in the dry desert
questions.explanation: Thick stems store water and the waxy skin slows water loss in the desert.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a cactus is a living water bottle!

questions.question: What is the main source of energy for almost all food chains?
questions.explanation: Sunlight powers photosynthesis, which starts nearly every food chain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Sun is the battery for almost all life!

questions.question: Which of these is a predator?
questions.explanation: A predator hunts and eats other animals, like an owl hunting mice.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: predators hunt - prey hides!

questions.question: What happens when a population grows too large for its habitat?
questions.correctAnswer: Some organisms run out of food or space
questions.explanation: Too many organisms means not enough food, water, or space for all of them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: too many dinos, not enough snacks - something has to give!

questions.question: Why are bees important to many plants?
questions.correctAnswer: Bees move pollen so plants can make seeds
distractors: Bees dig holes for plant roots
questions.explanation: As bees visit flowers, they carry pollen from flower to flower, which lets plants reproduce.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: bees are the mail carriers of pollen!

questions.question: What is the water cycle?
questions.correctAnswer: Water moving between Earth and the sky by evaporation, condensation, and precipitation
distractors: Water used by people in homes
questions.explanation: The water cycle is the endless loop of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: water travels up to the clouds and back down again!

questions.question: What is precipitation?
questions.correctAnswer: Water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
questions.explanation: Precipitation is any water that falls from the sky.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: precipitation is sky water falling down!

questions.question: What is condensation?
questions.correctAnswer: Water vapor cooling into tiny liquid drops
questions.explanation: When water vapor cools, it condenses into the tiny droplets that make clouds.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cool air squeezes vapor into cloud droplets!

questions.question: What causes wind?
questions.correctAnswer: Air moving from high pressure to low pressure
questions.explanation: Wind is air flowing from places with higher pressure toward places with lower pressure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wind is air rushing to fill the low-pressure spot!

questions.question: Which tool measures air temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the air is.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a thermometer tells you how hot or cold it is!

questions.question: Which tool measures rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects rain so you can measure how much fell.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a rain gauge is a cup that catches the rain!

questions.question: What does a barometer measure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures air pressure, which helps predict weather changes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a barometer feels how heavy the air is pressing down!

questions.question: What is the main cause of Earth's seasons?
distractors: Earth moving closer to the Sun in summer
questions.explanation: Earth's tilted axis means different parts get more direct sunlight at different times of year.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the tilt is why summer is sunny and winter is chilly!

questions.question: Which layer of Earth do we live on?
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin, rocky outer layer where we live.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the crust is Earth's thin crunchy skin!

questions.question: What is the center of Earth called?
questions.explanation: The core is the hot center, with a liquid outer core and a solid inner core.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the core is Earth's super-hot heart!

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest ocean, covering more area than all Earth's land combined.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Pacific is so big it could swallow all the land!

questions.question: What is groundwater?
questions.correctAnswer: Water stored underground in soil and rock
questions.explanation: Groundwater is water that soaks down and is stored in cracks and spaces underground.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: groundwater hides in the spaces under your feet!

questions.question: What is erosion?
questions.correctAnswer: Soil and rock being worn away and moved by water, wind, or ice
questions.explanation: Erosion moves weathered rock and soil to new places.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: erosion is nature slowly carrying the land away!

questions.question: Which of these causes the most erosion in a river valley?
questions.explanation: Fast-moving river water wears away banks and carries soil downstream.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rushing water carves valleys like a slow chisel!

questions.question: What is weathering?
questions.correctAnswer: Rock breaking down into smaller pieces where it sits
distractors: Rock being carried to a new place
Rock turning into soil plants eat
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks rock apart in place; erosion then moves the pieces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: weathering cracks rocks - erosion carries the pieces away!

questions.question: What is energy?
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to do work or cause change
questions.explanation: Energy is what lets things move, heat up, light up, or change.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: energy is the power to make things happen!

questions.question: Which of these is a form of energy?
questions.explanation: Heat, light, sound, and motion are all forms of energy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: heat, light, and motion are all energy in action!

questions.question: What force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls everything toward Earth's center.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: gravity is Earth's invisible hug pulling everything down!

questions.question: What is friction?
questions.correctAnswer: A force that slows things down when surfaces rub together
distractors: A force that pulls objects up
questions.explanation: Friction resists motion between two touching surfaces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: friction is the rub that slows things down!

questions.question: Why do we use wheels on a cart?
questions.correctAnswer: Wheels reduce friction so the cart moves easily
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wheels turn a hard slide into an easy roll!

questions.question: What is a magnet attracted to?
questions.explanation: Magnets attract iron and a few other metals like nickel and cobalt.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: magnets love iron - they stick like best friends!

questions.question: What happens when two north poles of magnets face each other?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel and opposite poles attract.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: same poles push apart - north hates north!

questions.question: What is the unit used to measure force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons, named after Isaac Newton.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: force is measured in newtons - thank you, Isaac!

questions.question: A ball rolls farther on smooth ice than on rough grass. Why?
questions.correctAnswer: There is less friction on the smooth ice
distractors: The ball is heavier on grass
The wind pushes harder on ice
questions.explanation: Rough surfaces create more friction, which slows the ball faster.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: smooth means slippery - less friction, longer roll!

questions.question: Which simple machine is a seesaw?
questions.explanation: A seesaw is a lever: a bar that turns on a fixed point called a fulcrum.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a seesaw is a lever - push down here, up goes there!

questions.question: Which simple machine helps you lift a flag up a pole?
questions.explanation: A pulley changes the direction of a force so you can pull down to lift up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a pulley lets you pull down to lift things up!

questions.question: What is speed?
questions.correctAnswer: How fast something moves, distance divided by time
questions.explanation: Speed tells how much distance is covered in a certain time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: speed is distance divided by time - zoom!

questions.question: A car travels 120 miles in 2 hours. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = 120 miles divided by 2 hours = 60 miles per hour.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: divide the miles by the hours to find the speed!

questions.question: What kind of energy does a moving bicycle have?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: moving things carry kinetic energy!

questions.question: What kind of energy does a stretched rubber band have before it is let go?
questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy, waiting to be released.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a stretched band stores energy like a coiled spring!

questions.question: What is photosynthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: How plants make food using sunlight, water, and air
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar and oxygen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants cook their food with sunlight!

questions.question: Which part of a plant makes food?
questions.explanation: Leaves catch sunlight and hold the chlorophyll that powers photosynthesis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: leaves are the plant's solar-powered kitchens!

questions.question: What do roots do for a plant?
questions.correctAnswer: They take in water and hold the plant in the soil
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: roots drink water and hold on tight!

questions.question: What gas do plants take in from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants breathe in carbon dioxide and breathe out oxygen!

questions.question: What gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis releases oxygen, which animals need to breathe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants give us the oxygen we breathe - say thanks!

questions.question: What is the job of a flower?
questions.correctAnswer: To help the plant reproduce by making seeds
questions.explanation: Flowers attract pollinators and produce seeds for new plants.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: flowers are the plant's way of making baby plants!

questions.question: What is a seed?
questions.correctAnswer: A young plant in a protective case, ready to grow
questions.explanation: A seed holds a tiny plant plus stored food until conditions are right to grow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a seed is a baby plant packed with a lunchbox!

questions.question: What do seeds need to germinate and grow?
questions.correctAnswer: Water, air, and the right temperature
questions.explanation: Seeds need water, oxygen, and warmth to sprout; light matters after sprouting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: water plus air plus warmth wakes a seed up!

questions.question: Which part of the plant carries water from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explanation: The stem is the highway that moves water and food through the plant.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the stem is the plant's delivery highway!

questions.question: What is the life cycle of a butterfly?
questions.explanation: A butterfly hatches as a caterpillar (larva), forms a chrysalis (pupa), then becomes an adult.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly - a four-step costume change!

questions.question: What is metamorphosis?
questions.correctAnswer: A big change in body shape as an animal grows
distractors: An animal moving to a new home
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is the change from larva to adult, like a tadpole becoming a frog.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: metamorphosis is nature's biggest makeover!

questions.question: Why do some animals hibernate in winter?
questions.correctAnswer: To save energy when food is scarce and it is cold
questions.explanation: Hibernation slows the body down so the animal can survive winter on stored fat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hibernation is a long winter nap to save energy!

questions.question: What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Vertebrates have a backbone and invertebrates do not
distractors: Vertebrates live on land and invertebrates live in water
Vertebrates eat meat and invertebrates eat plants
questions.explanation: The backbone is the key difference: fish, birds, and mammals are vertebrates; worms and insects are not.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: backbone or no backbone - that is the big split!

questions.question: Which of these is an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: An earthworm has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: no backbone, no problem - worms are invertebrates!

questions.question: How do fish get oxygen from water?
questions.explanation: Gills pull dissolved oxygen out of the water as it flows over them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: gills are fish lungs that work underwater!

questions.question: What is a fossil?
questions.correctAnswer: The remains or traces of an ancient living thing preserved in rock
distractors: A rock that fell from space
A bone from a living animal
questions.explanation: Fossils form when remains are buried and slowly turn to stone over millions of years.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fossils are ancient life turned to stone!

questions.question: What do fossils tell scientists?
questions.correctAnswer: What life was like long ago
distractors: What the weather will be tomorrow
questions.explanation: Fossils show which organisms lived in the past and how Earth has changed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fossils are Earth's old photo album!

questions.question: Which rock forms when lava or magma cools and hardens?
questions.explanation: Igneous rock, like granite and basalt, forms from cooled molten rock.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: igneous rock is born from fire - cooled lava!

questions.question: Which rock forms from layers of sand and mud pressed together?
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms when layers of sediment are compacted and cemented over time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sedimentary rock is layers squished into stone!

questions.question: What is the rock cycle?
questions.correctAnswer: Rocks changing from one type to another over time
distractors: Rocks being used to build houses
questions.explanation: Heat, pressure, melting, cooling, and weathering turn rocks from one type into another.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rocks recycle - igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic, round and round!

questions.question: In rock layers, which layer is usually the oldest?
distractors: They are all the same age
questions.explanation: New layers pile on top of older ones, so the bottom layer formed first.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the bottom layer is the oldest - like a stack of pancakes!

questions.question: What is the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot gas that makes its own light and heat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Sun is a star - our very own!

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mercury is first in line around the Sun!

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because of iron-rich dust on its surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mars is red like rusty iron dust!

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the biggest planet, more than twice as massive as all the others combined.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Jupiter is the giant of the planets!

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.explanation: As Earth spins, one side faces the Sun (day) while the other faces away (night).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's spin turns day into night!

questions.question: What causes the phases of the Moon?
questions.correctAnswer: The changing amount of the Moon's sunlit side we can see
questions.explanation: The Moon's lit side turns toward and away from us as it orbits Earth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Moon does not change shape - we just see different lit parts!

questions.question: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
questions.explanation: One trip around the Sun takes about 365 days, which is one year.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one lap around the Sun equals one year!

questions.question: What is the first step of the scientific method?
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a question or make an observation
questions.explanation: Science starts with a question about something you observed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: great science starts with a great question!

questions.question: What is a hypothesis?
questions.correctAnswer: An educated guess that can be tested
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a testable prediction based on what you already know.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a hypothesis is a smart guess you can test!

questions.question: In an experiment, what is the variable you change on purpose?
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one the scientist changes to see what happens.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the independent variable is the one YOU change!

questions.question: In an experiment, what do you measure to see the result?
questions.explanation: The dependent variable depends on what you changed, so you measure it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dependent variable is the result you measure!

questions.question: Why do scientists repeat an experiment?
questions.correctAnswer: To check that the results are reliable
questions.explanation: Repeating an experiment shows the result was not a one-time accident.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: repeat it to prove it was not a lucky accident!

questions.question: Which tool would you use to look at tiny cells?
questions.explanation: A microscope magnifies tiny things like cells so you can see them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a microscope makes tiny cells look huge!

questions.question: What is the best way to record what happens in an experiment?
questions.correctAnswer: Write down observations and measurements carefully
distractors: Guess the numbers at the end
Only write down the fun parts
questions.explanation: Careful notes let you compare results and share them with others.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: write it down - a good scientist never trusts memory alone!

questions.question: Which planet has beautiful rings made of ice and rock?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are made of chunks of ice and rock orbiting the planet.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Saturn wears rings of sparkling ice!

questions.question: Why does the Moon shine at night?
questions.explanation: The Moon has no light of its own; we see sunlight bouncing off it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Moon is a mirror for sunlight!

questions.question: What force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun's gravity pulls the planets, keeping them in orbit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Sun's gravity holds the planets in their lanes!
